8
A stone is thrown upwards and follows a curved path.
Air resistance is negligible.
Why does the path have this shape?
A
The stone has a constant horizontal acceleration and constant vertical velocity.
B
The stone has a constant horizontal velocity and constant vertical acceleration.
C
The stone has a constant upward acceleration followed by a constant downward acceleration.
D
The stone has a constant upward velocity followed by a constant downward velocity.

hints: Notice the stone in the diagram moves sideways and up-down at the same time, and air resistance is negligible so weight is the only force.
Recall what zero horizontal force implies for horizontal velocity, and what a constant downward weight implies for vertical acceleration $g$.
Compare steady motion sideways with uniformly slowing rise then speeding fall to see why the combined $x-t$ and $y-t$ motions make a smooth curve.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: the stone is projected with both horizontal and upward vertical velocity, and with negligible air resistance the only force is its weight acting vertically downwards.

Apply Newton's laws separately: horizontally $F_x = 0$ so $a_x = 0$ and horizontal velocity $v_x$ remains constant; vertically $F_y = mg$ downwards so vertical acceleration is constant $a = g$ downwards.
Describe the effect on velocity: $v_x$ is unchanged through the flight, while vertical velocity $v_y = u_y - gt$ decreases to zero at the peak and then becomes increasingly negative on the way down.
Combine the two independent motions: equal sideways steps in equal times plus smaller upward steps then larger downward steps traces out the symmetric curved parabola shown.
Only constant horizontal velocity with constant vertical acceleration matches this cause-and-effect chain. This is option B.

A.explanation: This swaps the directions. There is no horizontal force so horizontal acceleration is zero, while vertical velocity changes continuously.

B.explanation: With negligible air resistance, horizontal velocity stays constant and vertical motion has constant downward acceleration $g$, whose combination gives the curved parabolic path.

C.explanation: Acceleration does not change from up to down at the top. It is constant and downwards at about $9.81 \text{m s}^{-2}$ for the whole flight.

D.explanation: Vertical velocity is not constant. It decreases to zero at the top of the curve and then increases downwards because of weight.
